<think>**Deriving bill-state logic**

**Factoring bill-next logic**

</think>

{
  "candidate_rtl": "module ticket_machine #(
    parameter ON  = 1'b1,
    parameter OFF = 1'b0
) (
    input  clk, clear, ten, twenty,
    output reg ready, dispense, return_sig, bill
);

    // Explicit one-hot state bits, plus a redundant registered bill decode.
    reg s_ready, s_disp, s_return;
    reg s_bill10, s_bill20, s_bill30;
    reg bill_q;

    wire take_ten    = ten;
    wire take_twenty = ~ten & twenty;
    wire hold_money  = ~ten & ~twenty;

    // Compute the bill indication for the state entered at this edge.
    // BILL10 always transitions to another bill state.
    wire next_bill = s_bill10
                   | (s_ready  & (ten | twenty))
                   | (s_bill20 & (ten | ~twenty))
                   | (s_bill30 & hold_money);

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (clear) begin
            s_ready  <= 1'b1;
            s_disp   <= 1'b0;
            s_return <= 1'b0;
            s_bill10 <= 1'b0;
            s_bill20 <= 1'b0;
            s_bill30 <= 1'b0;
            bill_q   <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            s_ready  <= s_disp | s_return | (s_ready & hold_money);
            s_bill10 <= (s_ready & take_ten)
                      | (s_bill10 & hold_money);
            s_bill20 <= (s_ready & take_twenty)
                      | (s_bill10 & take_ten)
                      | (s_bill20 & hold_money);
            s_bill30 <= (s_bill10 & take_twenty)
                      | (s_bill20 & take_ten)
                      | (s_bill30 & hold_money);
            s_disp   <= (s_bill20 & take_twenty)
                      | (s_bill30 & take_ten);
            s_return <= s_bill30 & take_twenty;
            bill_q   <= next_bill;
        end
    end

    always @* begin
        ready      = s_ready  ? ON : OFF;
        dispense   = s_disp   ? ON : OFF;
        return_sig = s_return ? ON : OFF;
        bill       = bill_q   ? ON : OFF;
    end

endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The measured worst path is the state-register-to-bill output path: 0.30 ns clock-to-Q plus 0.40 ns through the three-input OR, yielding 9.30 ns setup slack. The baseline already uses a synthesis-recoded one-hot FSM, so merely changing the state encoding is not a demonstrated remedy.",
  "rewrite": "Use explicit one-hot transition equations and add a redundant bill register. Its D input describes whether the next state is BILL10, BILL20 or BILL30. Consequently, bill is driven directly by a register for the default parameters, rather than by an OR of three state bits. The other outputs remain direct Moore state indications.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The targeted output path loses its three-input OR without adding output latency. The baseline's next reported register-to-register path has 9.38 ns slack, so eliminating the output bottleneck alone suggests approximately 0.08 ns of possible WNS improvement if internal timing remains comparable. The new bill-register input cone may instead become critical. No gain is measured or guaranteed; synthesis and STA must establish strictly improved WNS and non-regressed TNS.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Adds one flip-flop and a next-bill logic cone, with some possible sharing of transition logic. The explicit equations may also change mapping and fanout. Mapped area must be checked against the fixed 278.01664 um2 cap; compliance is not established without EDA.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the top interface and parameter declarations, synchronous active-high clear, single positive-edge clock, and output latency. After the specified reset, the six state bits remain one-hot and bill_q equals the OR of the three bill-state bits. Simultaneous ten and twenty retain ten priority. Every later clear assertion restores the ready state and clears bill_q at that same edge. No extra startup assumptions are introduced. Arbitrary illegal internal encodings before reset are not claimed equivalent; equivalence is required under the supplied fixed startup contract against the original frozen RTL."
}
